content:
The Bahrain Grand Prix will be streamed live for free on Apple TV this weekend, no subscription required. Interestingly, the Bahrain Grand Prix is actually being held at Sepang in Malaysia.

Normally, F1 races on Apple TV require a paid subscription to watch, but this weekend they are completely free for all viewers. You can catch up on the replayed qualifying session to prepare for tonight's live main race, which starts at 3:00 AM Eastern Time in the US.

All you need to do is download the Apple TV app on a compatible device, be in the United States, and stay up late to watch the live broadcast.

The race broadcast will begin at 1:50 AM Eastern Time, with the main race scheduled to start at 3:00 AM. Of course, if you want to go to bed early, you can also watch it later via the on-demand feature.

You can get the Apple TV app on Apple devices, Amazon Fire Stick, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox, Android and other platforms, or watch it via your browser at tv.apple.com.

With qualifying having taken place earlier, Red Bull's Max Verstappen secured pole position for the first time this season, with Lewis Hamilton in second and championship leader Kimi Antonelli in third. This is Red Bull's best chance at a title so far this season.

You may be wondering why the Bahrain Grand Prix is being held in Malaysia. Under normal circumstances, the Bahrain round usually takes place early in the season, but due to the ongoing war in Iran, the race was forced to be cancelled, and the Bahrain organisers decided instead to sponsor a race held elsewhere in the world.

Although Sepang is no longer part of the official F1 calendar, as a circuit beloved by fans, it is expected to deliver exciting on-track action for spectators.

A reminder again: use the Apple TV app to watch for free, no subscription required. The main race starts at 3:00 AM Eastern Time, with coverage beginning at 1:50 AM.
